dedupe_keys.name: simulation of supply chain disruptions after the great east japan earthquake considering establishments and power outages 2023

description: This case study simulates the economic loss from supply chain disruptions triggered by the Great East Japan Earthquake of 11 March 2011 and its tsunami, applying firm-level supply chain data and establishment-level attributes to an agent-based model. It extends earlier work in four ways: locating damage to production facilities with establishment census and survey data and GIS data on seismic intensity and tsunami height, capturing supply links of branch establishments, adding the effect of power outages on production in the weeks after the event, and using sector-specific parameters. It was produced by Hiroyasu Inoue, Yoshihiro Okumura, Tetsuya Torayashiki and Yasuyuki Todo and published in PLOS One on 7 July 2023. Coverage is Japan, with supply chains from Tokyo Shoko Research data on about one million firms. The article is available free under CC BY 4.0, and the model code is on GitHub, while the firm data are proprietary. Findings: the first three extensions markedly improved the prediction of domestic production after the earthquake, while sector-specific parameters added little. Caveats: agent-based models ignore price responses and input substitution, as the authors note, and the calibration cannot be reproduced without the licensed data. For simulation it shows how power outages amplify cascading supply chain losses and offers a method for regional scenarios such as a Nankai Trough earthquake. It is related to the Inoue production network simulator record in this catalogue, the code it uses.
